top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, a single writer in Romanian) is the only award proposal on the slate. On the common criteria and from public knowledge, his voice is recognisably his own. The Orbitor sequence (Blinding is its first volume) and Solenoid appear to build memory, the body and dream into one cumulative metaphysical project of large formal ambition. The major structures already exist, so the oeuvre can be assessed now. Attribution is clean, and the prose-centred citation, which names the poetry only as foundation, claims no more than the evidence supports. I find no literary ground in the round-2 exchange to prefer P000, because the reservations concern verification and translation, not demonstrated shortcomings. These reservations remain open. Romanian sentence-level density and rhythm are judged only indirectly, and whether the later volumes advance the project or only enlarge it is unverified. I have not read the corpus independently or verified sources. Unanimity in the openings is not evidence of merit, so I rest this ranking on the work and its design. P000 is ranked second as the fallback if Romanian-reading expert assessment showed loss of control or repetition.
